definition: Pain the senior reports or shows. Body site kept as said. No intensity scale.
How the senior slept, as described by her or observed.
A visible change on the skin (redness, bruise, wound, rash) as described, with site. No staging or grading.
Shortness of breath observed or reported.
Dizziness the senior reports.
An episode of urine or stool leakage.
Bowel movements as described (e.g. constipation reported).
Difficulty hearing, observed or reported.
Difficulty seeing, observed or reported.
A problem with teeth, gums or dentures, as described.
Blood pressure measured during the visit (or on the senior's own device). Numbers only; no reference range.
Heart rate measured during the visit. Number only.
Blood glucose from the senior's meter, as read. Number only.
Body temperature measured during the visit. Number only.
Anything about physical state that no other concept fits. Reviewed monthly.
The senior's mood in everyday words.
What the senior talked about.
Who called or visited.
Confusion or a memory lapse, described in words. Never labelled as dementia or any condition.
The senior said she feels lonely.
An activity the senior enjoyed or took part in.
Something the senior said she would like.
Anything about mood, memory or social life that no other concept fits.
The caregiver gave medication. Time and name as said; no dose checking.
The senior took her medication by herself.
The senior declined a medication. Recorded neutrally.
A dose was missed (e.g. found untaken in the organiser).
The caregiver filled or prepared the pill organiser.
Anything about medication that no other concept fits.
A meal and how much of it was eaten. Portion only if said.
How much the senior drank: a number if said, otherwise a word.
Appetite, only as compared by the caregiver or senior.
Body weight if weighed. Number only.
Difficulty swallowing, observed or reported.
The caregiver prepared a meal.
Anything about eating or drinking that no other concept fits.
How the senior walked.
Getting in and out of bed or a chair.
The caregiver went for a walk with the senior. Destination as said.
Unsteadiness or a near-fall. An actual fall is an outcome event, not this.
The senior went outside.
Exercises done with the caregiver.
Anything about moving around that no other concept fits.
Washing or bathing. As an observation: how much help was needed. As a care activity: its outcome (done / declined…).
Dressing; same two uses as bathing.
Using the toilet; same two uses as bathing.
Oral care or denture care.
Hair, nails, shaving.
The caregiver changed incontinence products.
Anything about personal care that no other concept fits.
The caregiver cleaned.
The caregiver did laundry.
The caregiver aired the rooms.
A problem with heating or temperature at home.
Something at home that could cause harm (loose rug, gas smell…), as described.
A broken appliance or fitting.
Anything about the home that no other concept fits.
The caregiver did the shopping.
An errand run (post office, pharmacy…), as said.
A prescription or medication was collected.
A planned appointment (doctor, office…). An urgent one is an outcome event.
A planned appointment took place.
Help with documents or forms.
Help with bills or payments.
The caregiver drove or accompanied the senior somewhere.
Help with a phone call or other contact.
Any errand or matter that no other concept fits.
